newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent, gas oil to kick off 1997 sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent, gas oil to kick off 1997 sharply higher.

text.p: IPE Brent and gas oil futures are expected to begin 1997 trading sharply higher as a prolonged spell of freezing weather in Europe boosts demand for heating fuel, dealers said.
IPE Jan gas oil (heating oil), which settled at $223.75 a tonne on Tuesday, was expected to open anywhere between $3-$5 a tonne higher on Thursday, they said.
Feb Brent crude traded at $24.15 a barrel in Singapore, 34 cents above its London settlement.
"We're expecting gas oil to come in $3-$4 a tonne higher but it could be as much as $5 or $6," said a London broker.
"I'm told its minus 15 (degrees Centigrade) in Belgium this morning so the barge market players won't be selling this," he added.
NYMEX heating oil rallied late on Tuesday on a combination of short-covering ahead of the January contract's expiry and the prolonged cold snap in Europe, U.S. dealers said.
"Heating oil surged despite warmer weather entering the U.S. East Coast, with freezing temperatures in Europe the main driving force," said London brokers GNI in a daily report.
Forecasters see no quick end to the arctic conditions, which claimed at least seven lives in Britain over the New Year break.
Private U.S. forecaster Weather Services Corp (WSC) said strong easterly winds would continue to promote low temperatures and high energy demand at least until Saturday.
"Temperatures will be below normal during the extended period," WSC added.
Despite this week's rally, both Brent and gas oil remain some way below their recent record highs of $25.06 a barrel and $250.00 a tonne posted in October last year.
